newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S-E-Banken says no deal reached with Nordbanken.
newsitem.headline: S-E-Banken says no deal reached with Nordbanken.

text.p: S-E-Banken Managing Director Jacob Wallenberg denied in an internal newsletter, a copy of which was received by Reuters on Monday, that the bank had reached an accord with Nordbanken.

"I would like to firmly deny what has been written in Svenska Dagbladet and Dagens Industri (daily newspapers) that an accord or agreement has been reached with Nordbanken. In general I cannot and will not comment on the various media reports," he said.

The newspapers carried reports at the weekend that Nordbanken was close to reaching a comprehensive cooperation agreement with S-E-Banken in which it would take over S-E-Banken's nationwide network of bank offices.
The reports, citing unnamed sources, also said S-E-Banken would buy the Nordbanken operations and become a merchant bank.
S-E-Banken would not confirm or deny that talks had taken place with Nordbanken.
Wallenberg said in the newsletter the bank was working with structural questions and talks with other partners were part of that process.

"I have been saying since I took this post that I am working with the questions regarding the bank's structure and vision. This work has been going on at full steam and naturally includes contact with other partners from time to time," he said.
"I have also said that I believe in an increased focus, that in time we will be good at doing all things for everyone," Wallenberg said.
Wallenberg said the bank was not in a hurry to find a solution to restructuring questions.
"There are several possibilities and we are not in a hurry," Wallenberg said.
